Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image render the depicted forms as a drawing rather than retaining substantial photographic detail beneath drawn contours?
node.criteria: Pass if, compared with the source, the depicted forms are visibly rendered as drawn forms, with drawing-like contours or linework and without substantial photographic surface detail remaining. Fail if the image retains substantial photographic representation even where outlines or linework are added. Unknown only if the relevant representation cannot be observed.
node.source_quote: Turn the image into a drawing
node.endpoint: The depicted forms are rendered as a drawing rather than retaining substantial photographic representation.
node.necessity: The instruction requests turning the image into a drawing; outlines alone do not establish that transformation when the depicted forms still retain substantial photographic detail.

node_traces.evidence: Compared with the source photograph, the edited image renders the giraffes and surroundings with soft, grainy chalk-like shading and drawn contours; photographic surface detail in the animals, foliage, and ground is substantially reduced.

d2: The node’s criterion is already specific and the trace is grounded in visible changes: the edited image has broad smudged tonal strokes and sketchy, textured outlines across the scene, not merely added grain. However, the trace’s high-confidence “pass” conflicts with the aggregate reference “partial.” Do not resolve this by weakening the chalk requirement or treating low confidence/variation as evidence of absence. Clarify the decision boundary between visible chalk-like rendering and complete fulfillment of the overall instruction, and ensure this node reports only its own surface-rendering evidence; the aggregate should account for any other requested changes. The source and edit support chalk-like surface treatment, so investigate whether the reference’s partial label reflects a separate unmet requirement or an aggregation/routing issue. Keep the comparison anchored to the source and distinguish chalk-like marks from generic filtering.
